newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wholesale inflation remains subdued in Aug.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wholesale inflation remains subdued in Aug.

text.p: Inflation at the wholesale level remains subdued despite increased pressure from rising food and energy prices, U.S. experts said.
The Labor Department reported August U.S. producer prices were up 0.3 percent. The core rate was down 0.1 percent.

"The overall inflation picture appears good," said Peter Kretzmer, an economist at NationsBank Corp. "We don't see anything in the core numbers to indicate a long term increase...or underlying rate of inflation."
Although U.S. analysts agree the PPI report was favorable, rising food and energy prices may lead to short-run concerns.
"Rising gasoline and fuel oil definitely skewed the headline number but the fact that the core is down 0.1 pct is good news for the market," said Waldo Best, senior economist at BZW Securities Inc.
In the energy component of the report gasoline rose 0.9 percent while heating oil was up 4.1 percent, Labor said.

"There is a little bit of bad news, however," Best added. "Energy is already starting to move up and we really haven't seen the effects of the current energy prices which have been building up over the past two to three months."
Food prices were up 1.0 percent in August while intermediate goods were up by 0.2 percent, Labor reported.
"It's a decent number. The strength in food prices is a bit unexpected but the core PPI rate is very subdued," said David Sloan, senior economist at I.D.E.A. Inc.

"Prices at the crude and intermediate stages of production don't provide much strength. We've actually seen a fall in food prices at the crude level so the increase in food prices probably will not be sustained. The energy prices will be sustained due to the situation in Iraq," Sloan added.
Economists said that while the report contained some reassuring elements, the rise in food and energy prices will leadto some concerns going forward.
"Food and energy prices will be problematic for the rest of the year," BZW's Best said.
Meanwhile, U.S. experts will focus on Friday's key release of the Consumer Price Index for August for a look at inflation at the consumer level.
